Friday the 13th proved to be a productive reading day.

- I started with a refresh- read of
  [Ankley's](https://doi.org/10.1002/etc.34) (and 11 others in 2010) AOP
  paper.

- Moved to [Abdel-Shafy &
  Mansour's](https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S1110062114200237)
  2016 PAH Review.

- Closed with
  [Damien's](https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0045653506006965)
  (et al., 2007) Integrated Biomarker Response paper.

  - My purpose was to get back into daily reading with concepts I am
    already familiar with. This time, I'm reading for application to my
    work, not only as background knowledge gain- which was the first
    time I read each. Shifting purpose means a different critical
    reading and note taking.

I shifted to grading the Nature Essay Final Drafts

- I'm about a third of the way through and will pick back up tomorrow to
  have grades ready for release by Sunday night.

Before returning to the biomarker re-analysis, I spent some time
clarifying the methylation results I write previously.

- I drafted the results fairly broadly, so I went back and asked myself
  to answer these questions about each loci or each group (hypo- or
  hyper- methylated):

  - What is the molecular structure around the loci and what is the
    potential biological outcome attached to it?

  - If this specific loci is methylated in a gene, what do we think is
    the biological result?

- It feels pretty basic, but it was an on-ramp task to get back into the
  thought and writing I need to complete to get this draft out.
